turns.t: Hi there, take a seat. I see on the booking you wrote, white patches spreading. Tell me in your own words what's been happening.
There's white patches on my hands. They're getting bigger.
Okay. When did you first spot the white patches?
About six months ago.
Six months. And where did the first one show up?
The back of my right hand. Now there's some on the left too.
And more recently, have new ones appeared on other parts of your body?
Elbows. A few weeks back.
I see. Does it bother you in any physical way, like itching or soreness, or is it more about how it looks?
Mostly how it looks.
That's a very reasonable thing to be bothered by. People often tell me the appearance is the hardest part.
Yeah. I'm a guy who wears short sleeves in summer. People ask.
Of course. I'd like to take a proper look in a moment, and my nurse is going to help with a special lamp. Before that, let's get your numbers. Janet, could you wrap the cuff on his arm?
Sure thing. Roll your sleeve up for me, sir. Okay, sitting nice and still.
Blood pressure is 118 over 76. Pulse 66. Temperature 36.6 degrees. Respiratory rate 14. Oxygen saturation 99 percent, and your weight is 71 kilograms.
Is that good?
Those are all healthy numbers. Now Janet is going to switch off the main light and bring the lamp over.
Lights going off. This is a black light, it won't hurt, you'll just see a purple glow.
Cool.
Hold your hands out, palms down. I'm looking at each patch under the lamp now.
Under the lamp the patches on both hands and the elbows are chalk-white with very sharp edges. That's a typical appearance.
What does that mean?

Let me explain my reasoning. Skin gets its colour from cells called melanocytes. In these patches, those cells have stopped making pigment, and the skin turns white. The sharp edges and the symmetrical pattern on both hands are what point me in one direction.
Which direction?
This looks like vitiligo. It's a fairly common condition, and it happens when the immune system mistakenly targets the pigment cells.
Is it contagious?
Not at all, you can shake hands, share towels, whatever you like. It's also not caused by anything you ate or did.
My cousin said it's from stress.
Stress can sometimes coincide with a flare, but it's not the root cause. Janet, you can put the lights back on. Thanks.
Back on. Anything else you need from me, doctor?

Could you print the leaflet on sun protection for him? Thanks. Now, one more piece of my reasoning. Vitiligo is sometimes seen together with thyroid problems, so I'd like to order a thyroid blood test.
Okay. Today?
Today, Janet can take you through to the phlebotomy room after this. It's a quick one.
Fine.
The patches are very exposed to sun, because those cells don't protect the skin anymore. So please use a high factor sunscreen on your hands and elbows, especially in summer, or you'll burn.
I can do that.
Treatment options exist, creams and light therapy among them, and we'll talk about those properly when the blood results are back. I don't want to rush you into anything.
Sounds good. Thanks for explaining it.
I'd like to see you again in six weeks, so we can go over the results and decide on a plan together.
Six weeks. Got it.
I'll book you in at the desk on the way out, with the leaflet.
Perfect. Any other questions before you go?
Nope. That's it.
Good. See you soon, and take care of that skin.

physical_examination.finding: patches on both hands and the elbows are chalk-white with very sharp edges
physical_examination.normalized_finding: Sharply demarcated depigmented patches on hands and elbows

clinical_actions.description: Use high factor sunscreen on hands and elbows
